title: Standardize consumer shim and graceful throttling for async pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 12 months we've accumulated multiple ad-hoc consumer implementations for Redis and Kafka workers. Differences in retry semantics, ack/visibility handling, and shutdown/backpressure behavior have caused: occasional duplicate work, priority inversion under burst load, and long tail latency when downstream services are degraded. This ticket scopes a cross-cutting refactor to introduce a lightweight consumer shim library and standardized throttling/circuit patterns that can be adopted by both Redis (list/pop/ack style) and Kafka consumers.

Goals: 1) Provide a single consumer shim API that enforces: at-most-once/at-least-once modes selectable per queue; idempotency token propagation; structured retry with exponential backoff + jitter; and cooperative graceful shutdown. 2) Implement an application-level backpressure mechanism (token-bucket ingress + dynamic concurrency cap) to bound CPU/memory under bursts and to protect downstream services. 3) Add a small circuit-breaker and retry budget tracker to avoid retry storms when third-party services fail. 4) Ship with feature flags/canary rollout and migration tooling to convert existing workers incrementally. 5) Improve observability: per-queue metrics (processing time, retry rate, dropped/failed count), tracing hooks for rebalances and visibility-extension events, and an alert baseline.

Design decisions and trade-offs: - Single shim vs separate libraries: a single shim with pluggable adapters (RedisAdapter, KafkaAdapter) reduces duplication but requires careful API boundaries so teams don't bypass it. We chose pluggable adapters to balance adoption friction. - Retry semantics: default to at-least-once with idempotency token header; provide at-most-once mode for latency-sensitive queues. - Backpressure strategy: token-bucket ingress combined with a dynamic concurrency cap (guided by P95 latency and CPU) chosen over hard queue-length based throttles because it adapts to varying worker speeds and cloud burstiness. - Visibility semantics for Redis: use a lazy-renew approach for long-running tasks (extend visibility only on heartbeat milestones) to avoid hot loops renewing visibility every second.

Implementation plan: Phase A (prototype, non-breaking): build consumer-shim core + RedisAdapter; implement token-bucket ingress and a concurrency controller; unit tests and integration tests in staging. Phase B (KafkaAdapter + canary): implement KafkaAdapter with cooperative rebalancing hooks; run canary on low-traffic queues for 2 weeks, gather metrics. Phase C (migrate): enable feature-flagged rollout for mid/low-risk queues, add migration checklist for high-risk queues (workflows with side effects).

Progress updates (chronological): - 2026-02-26: Spike completed (A. Patel, M. Rivera): prototype shim + Redis adapter; simple token-bucket implemented; basic unit tests added. Initial benchmark vs current Redis consumer shows 12% lower CPU tail at 99th percentile for small payloads and 8% lower median latency under steady load. Link to spike notes: https://docs.internal.redwood/spikes/consumer-shim-prototype.
- 2026-03-03: Design review with platform team: accepted pluggable adapter approach; ops requested configurability for per-queue concurrency caps and a migration mode that can auto-roll back on increased error rates. Added to backlog.
- 2026-03-07: Implemented circuit-breaker and retry-budget tracker; integration tests for exponential backoff with jitter passed in CI. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321.
- 2026-03-10: Canary run started for redis-analytics-queue (10% traffic). Early telemetry: retry-rate down 18%, average worker concurrency reduced by 22% with no customer-visible increase in latency. Noted an unexpected interaction with the legacy visibility timeout extension in payments-processor worker; added a compatibility shim option to disable lazy renew for that queue.
- 2026-03-12: Blocked on ops approval for rolling out KafkaAdapter in staging due to required Kafka client upgrade (client 3.1 -> 3.4). Ticket opened to upgrade Kafka client dependency with compatibility testing.

Open tasks / next steps: 1) Finish KafkaAdapter implementation and run integration tests against staging cluster (owner: J. Kim). 2) Coordinate Kafka client upgrade (owner: SRE - ENG-10689) and verify rebalance stability with our cooperative shutdown hooks. 3) Add end-to-end migration playbook and a per-queue risk scorecard to help PMs prioritize migrations. 4) Add a small migration support tool to scan repos for direct consumer usage and suggest adapter wiring changes. 5) Expand canary to additional queues (search-indexing and notifications) once Kafka client upgrade is complete.

Rollout and rollback plan: - Default to disabled via feature flag. Enable shim in canary mode (10% of traffic) for one queue and monitor retry rate, processing latency, and error budget for 14 days. If retry rate increases by >30% or P95 latency increases by >20%, auto-roll back the flag. For high-risk queues, use manual ops window and pre-check idempotency.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for shim API, adapter edge cases, and visibility-renew edge conditions. - Integration tests in staging with fault injection (downstream service error, network partitions) to validate circuit-breaker and retry budget enforcement. - Performance benchmark harness: run existing load profiles (producer patterns A/B/C) and compare CPU/latency/cost.

PRs and artifacts: - Draft implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321 - Design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/design/consumer-shim-and-backpressure - Spike notes and perf graphs: https://docs.internal.redwood/spikes/consumer-shim-prototype - Migration checklist template: https://docs.internal.redwood/playbooks/consumer-migration-checklist

Risks and mitigations: - Kafka client upgrade may introduce client-side rebalance changes; mitigation: coordinate with SRE, run a dedicated cluster with upgraded client and run rebalance stress tests. - Teams bypassing shim: mitigation: add lint rule and a CI check to detect direct consumer core usage, and a migration support bot to open PR suggestions. - Incorrect default configs causing throughput regression: mitigation: conservative defaults, clear docs, per-queue overrides, and staged canaries.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Shim library published to internal package registry with RedisAdapter and KafkaAdapter. 2) Two queues (one Redis, one Kafka) successfully migrated behind feature flags with no customer-visible regressions and documented rollback steps. 3) Observability: per-queue metrics and tracing hooks in place and dashboards updated. 4) Kafka client upgraded in staging and no regressions in rebalance stability.

Notes: related prior tickets ENG-7421 and ENG-9187 provided valuable context on backpressure and async queue topology; this ticket aims to consolidate patterns and provide a maintainable library rather than duplicating fixes per-service.

Review feedback snippets: - PM: “We need a clear migration signal in the console so product owners can see which queues are on the shim.” Action: add console flag exposure and per-queue risk in the rollout plan. - SRE: “Make sure shutdown hooks integrate with our drain protocol.” Action: add a drain adapter that delegates to shim graceful shutdown with a max wait timeout.
